input.plainEnglish: Press the use key and the game looks once, along your aim. The look is a question you asked. It is not something the pawn keeps asking while you stand still.
input.whyGame: A first-person door, a light switch, and a weapon on the floor all wait for that one press. If the trace moves onto Tick, every idle player spends a physics query and the stored hit is already stale when the key finally goes down.

expansions.title: A door
expansions.detail: The door implements Interact. The true pin of the use trace calls it, and the door swings if it is unlocked.

expansions.title: A switch
expansions.detail: The switch is the same interface. The hit flips a bool. It does not need its own trace.

expansions.title: A floor weapon
expansions.detail: The press can find the weapon, but adding it to the inventory is a different graph. The look only reports the hit.

quiz.prompt: Which node starts the interact graph when the player presses the use key?
choices: The Enhanced Input node bound to IA_Interact
Spawning should trace once and then never look again
Standing still should keep tracing every frame
A replicated health change should be what opens doors
quiz.why: The press is the start. Tick is not in this graph.

quiz.prompt: The generated function Graph_IA_Interact_tpl_interact_input runs. What did the player just do?
choices: Pressed the bound use control, on keyboard or pad
Took damage from another player
Overlapped a pickup volume
Finished loading a save slot
quiz.why: That function is the use action. It is not damage, overlap, or a load.

quiz.prompt: The line trace in the interact graph returns a bool. Which node reads that bool next?
choices: Branch, whose true pin continues only when something was hit
A successful look should add rounds to the magazine
A successful look should set how fast you sprint
A hit bool should be packed into the save file
quiz.why: The hit bool is the branch condition.

quiz.prompt: You move the interact trace onto Tick so the use prompt never feels late. What goes wrong?
choices: Every idle pawn pays for a query
The mapping context stops accepting the keyboard
IA_Interact can no longer be rebound to a gamepad
Doors lose their mesh
quiz.why: The press already asks at the right time. Tick asks when nobody did.

quiz.prompt: A player rebinds use from F to a gamepad face button. What stays the same in the graph?
choices: IA_Interact still fires Triggered
The trace must be rewritten to mention the new key code
Branch has to compare the raw key instead of the hit
Begin Play must register the button on the door actor
quiz.why: The graph never reads the key code.

quiz.prompt: Where is the mapping context added for this use action?
choices: On the possessed pawn or the player controller
On every door Blueprint, so each door knows the key
Inside the save struct, so the binding reloads as a float
On the magazine component
quiz.why: The pawn or controller owns input. The door only implements Interact.

quiz.prompt: The interact trace should run when the use action fires, not from Tick.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The trace runs from the action.

quiz.prompt: True or false: one mapping context can bind the same use action to a key and a pad.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is what a mapping context is for.

quiz.prompt: Why does the true pin call an interface instead of casting to every usable Blueprint?
choices: A door, a switch, and a weapon can all answer one Interact call
A cast is illegal on a line trace result
Interfaces skip the branch and always open the door
The false pin needs an interface or the miss will not log
quiz.why: One call stays stable as you add usable actors.

quiz.prompt: True or false: a miss on the use trace should still open the door in front of the camera.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The false pin is a miss. It stops.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does the look start from the use key instead of Tick?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What happens to a door or a floor weapon if every idle pawn traces on Tick?

movement.plainEnglish: Push the stick and the pawn stores a sprint speed. Release it and the pawn stores a walk speed. The character movement component reads that number. The graph does not shove the actor along the world axis every frame.
movement.whyGame: If Speed is written from Tick, a stance or an ability that just set a different speed gets stomped before the animation can show it. The camera and the weapon read this pawn. They do not own Speed.

expansions.title: Crouch
expansions.detail: Crouch can write a third speed from its own action. It should not share the Tick that this graph refuses to use.

expansions.title: Aim slowdown
expansions.detail: While aiming, a later lesson can scale Speed. The move graph still only writes when the axis changes.

expansions.title: Data speeds
expansions.detail: 600 and 200 are sample literals. A data row can replace them without moving the write onto Tick.

quiz.prompt: What does the move action write into the pawn?
choices: Speed, which character movement then consumes
Sprinting should spend hit points instead of storing a speed
Running should refill the magazine
Pushing the stick should rewrite the save struct
quiz.why: Speed is the gait number.

quiz.prompt: Graph_IA_Move_tpl_movement_input assigns either 600 or 200. What chooses between them?
choices: Whether the stick axis is greater than zero
Whether the pawn currently has authority
Whether OnRep_Health has run this frame
Whether the interact trace hit a door
quiz.why: A pushed stick is greater than zero and takes the sprint literal.

quiz.prompt: After Greater Than, which node must run before Speed actually changes?
choices: Branch, so the true path and the false path can set different literals
The floor should be traced to decide sprint versus walk
Sprinting should deal damage to the pawn
Last frame's speed should be reloaded from the save
quiz.why: The comparison only picks a path. Set Speed is on those paths.

quiz.prompt: Speed is assigned from Tick so the gait never misses a frame. What gets stomped?
choices: A speed an ability or a stance just wrote
The player's key bindings
The reload clamp gets wiped
The door's swing curve is what gets reset
quiz.why: Tick does not know that something else already set Speed.

quiz.prompt: The player lets go of the stick in a doorway. Which value has to win?
choices: The walk literal on the false path
Sprint speed should stick until the next shot
Letting go of the stick should drop health to zero
An empty stick should holster the current weapon
quiz.why: Released axis is the walk write.

quiz.prompt: The camera and the weapon both care how fast the pawn moves. Should they write Speed?
choices: No. They read the pawn. Only the move action writes Speed
The aim trace should overwrite speed because it sees the world
Firing should force a sprint so the shot feels fast
Only a loaded save may choose walk or sprint
quiz.why: Neighbors read. They do not own this variable.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Speed is written when the move axis changes, not from Tick.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The axis is the event.

quiz.prompt: True or false: the false path of the move branch should leave Speed at the sprint value.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The false path writes the walk literal.

quiz.prompt: A designer later replaces 600 and 200 with a data row. What part of the graph stays?
choices: The axis comparison and the two Set Speed nodes
A Tick that samples the data row every frame
A cast to every movement Blueprint
An OnRep that rewrites Speed when health changes
quiz.why: The numbers move to data. The write stays on the axis.

quiz.prompt: True or false: adding a world offset on Tick is how this lesson moves the pawn.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Character movement reads Speed. The graph does not shove the actor.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does the stick write sprint or walk speed instead of Tick overwriting Speed?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What breaks in the animation if Tick stomps a stance that just set a different speed?

interaction.plainEnglish: The use trace finds an actor and calls Interact. The door, the switch, and the dropped gun each implement that one call. You do not cast to their Blueprints.
interaction.whyGame: A cast list grows every time a new usable actor ships. An interface stays one call. The hunter's Sense trace, if you are thinking of horror, is a different graph and must not be pasted here.

expansions.title: Locked door
expansions.detail: Interact can check a key and refuse. The refusal stays inside the door, not in a new trace.

expansions.title: Button
expansions.detail: A button is another Interact. It flips its own state.

expansions.title: Note pickup
expansions.detail: A readable note can answer Interact by opening text. The trace still only reports the hit.

quiz.prompt: One interface serves every usable actor in this lesson. What call is that?
choices: Interact, on whatever the use trace hit
Giving the door an inventory stack instead of opening it
Treating the door like a selected strategy unit
Treating the use key as a gameplay effect
quiz.why: Interact is the shared contract.

quiz.prompt: The interact call reaches ProcessEvent on the name Interact. What does that line mean in play?
choices: The hit actor runs its own Interact, if it has one
Every Blueprint in the level runs Interact
The magazine reloads because the name sounds like use
Health is subtracted by the length of the name
quiz.why: ProcessEvent looks up that function on the hit actor only.

quiz.prompt: The trace hits a door. What has to happen before Execute Interact?
choices: Branch takes the true pin because the hit bool is set
Set Speed writes 600 so the door opens faster
Begin Play runs again
The save struct is broken apart
quiz.why: A miss must not call the door.

quiz.prompt: You add a cast to BP_Door, BP_Switch, and BP_Gun beside the trace. What grows on the next usable actor?
choices: The cast list, one new node per Blueprint
Casts already discover the interface without a new node
Only the input mapping
The replicated health float
quiz.why: That list is the cost the interface avoids.

quiz.prompt: A level has a locked door and a live grenade, both usable. How does the use graph stay one trace?
choices: Both actors implement Interact and do their own work
The trace casts to the grenade first and the door on the false pin
Tick alternates between the two classes
The save file stores which class the trace prefers
quiz.why: The graph does not name the classes.

quiz.prompt: Sense, the hunter look from the horror lessons, is not this graph. Why must it stay out?
choices: The player's use is a press. The hunter's look is a timer
Sense is the only legal way to open a door
Interact cannot be called unless Alert is 1
A use trace without Sense will not compile
quiz.why: Different questions, different events.

quiz.prompt: True or false: one Interact call can serve a door, a switch, and a dropped weapon.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the point of the interface.

quiz.prompt: True or false: the false pin of the use branch should call Interact anyway.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: False means miss.

quiz.prompt: A new ladder Blueprint arrives. What do you add to the use graph?
choices: Nothing, if the ladder implements Interact
A cast to the ladder placed before the trace
A second trace that only hits ladders
A Tick that searches for ladder actors
quiz.why: The graph is already finished for any Interact actor.

quiz.prompt: True or false: the use graph should read the raw key code so rebinding needs a code change.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The mapping context owns the binding.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does the use trace call Interact instead of casting to each usable actor?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What fails when a new usable prop ships and the cast list was never edited?

weapon.plainEnglish: Reload asks two questions: is there room in the magazine, and is there ammo in reserve? Only then does Needed move rounds from reserve into the mag. Both checks happen on the reload key, not on Tick.
weapon.whyGame: Adding Needed inside Tick fills the gun while the player is sprinting or looking at a menu. Skipping the clamp loads more rounds than the magazine can hold, or more than the player is carrying.

expansions.title: Empty reload
expansions.detail: If reserve is zero the false pin logs and stops. It does not play a successful reload.

expansions.title: Chamber
expansions.detail: A later lesson can add a chambered round as another number. It still should not tick the magazine.

expansions.title: Shell type
expansions.detail: Buckshot versus slug can be a data row the reload reads. The checks stay on IA_Reload.

quiz.prompt: Both checks pass before a round moves. What are the two checks?
choices: Magazine is below MagSize
Speed is 600, and the trace hit a pawn
Health is full, and the save slot is loaded
The pawn has no authority, and Tick has run
quiz.why: Room in the mag, and something in reserve.

quiz.prompt: Needed = Clamp(Reserve, 0, MagSize - Magazine). What does that line keep from happening?
choices: Loading more rounds than the mag can hold or than you carry
The player aiming down sights
Health replicating to other clients
The interact trace missing a door
quiz.why: Needed is the legal transfer size.

quiz.prompt: Set Magazine adds Needed. What must already have run?
choices: The clamp, so Needed is a legal count
A health notify should refill the magazine
The patrol step should reload the player's gun
Visible = true, so fog allows ammo
quiz.why: Set Magazine without the clamp can overfill.

quiz.prompt: Magazine = Magazine + Needed sits inside Tick. What does the player see?
choices: The mag fills even when they did not press reload
Reload only when IA_Reload fires
Reserve climbing while the mag stays empty
The use trace starting a reload on a door
quiz.why: Tick does not know that a reload was requested.

quiz.prompt: Reserve is 4 and the mag has room for 12. After a correct reload, what moved?
choices: Four rounds, because Needed cannot exceed Reserve
Empty space wins and reserve is allowed to go negative
Waiting a full second of frames before any round moves
The equipped mesh, not the counts
quiz.why: The clamp caps Needed at Reserve.

quiz.prompt: The false pin of the reload branch logs that you cannot reload. When is that the right pin?
choices: The mag is already full, or the reserve is empty
The stick is released
The use trace missed
The pawn is the listen server
quiz.why: Either failed check refuses the transfer.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Set Magazine should run only after Needed has been clamped.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The clamp is the size of the move.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Reserve should increase by Needed when the magazine is filled.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Reserve loses the rounds the mag gained.

quiz.prompt: IA_Fire wants to share the reload function so one key does both. What should stay separate?
choices: Firing traces a shot. Reloading moves counts. They are different actions
They must share Tick or the mag desyncs
Fire should set Magazine to MagSize directly
Reload should call the interact interface
quiz.why: One event, one job.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Graph_IA_Reload runs because the player asked to reload.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The function is the reload action.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does reload ask about magazine room and reserve before it moves rounds?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What fills the gun at the wrong time if Needed is added from Tick?

health.plainEnglish: When this pawn takes damage, only the authority changes Health. Everyone else hears the new number and plays a reaction. They do not subtract again.
health.whyGame: If a client writes Health, the listen server and that client disagree about who is dead. If OnRep subtracts too, the proxy applies the hit twice and then snaps back when the real value arrives.

expansions.title: Armor
expansions.detail: Armor can be a second authority-owned number that damage spends first. Clients still only play the hit.

expansions.title: Regen
expansions.detail: Regen is a timer after the last hit, not a Tick that adds health every frame.

expansions.title: Downed
expansions.detail: At zero the authority can set a downed state. OnRep plays the fall. It does not decide the state.

quiz.prompt: Only the authority writes Health. What event should start that write?
choices: Any Damage, after Has Authority passes
Sprinting should be what starts a health change
The interact trace, because a door hit is damage
Spawn should set health and then freeze it forever
quiz.why: Damage is the event. Authority gates the float.

quiz.prompt: The line if (GetOwner() && GetOwner()->HasAuthority()) wraps the health assignment. Why ask the owner?
choices: A component is not the authority. The owning actor is
GetOwner returns the client with the lowest ping
The owner is the widget that draws the bar
HasAuthority is true only inside OnRep
quiz.why: The component asks its actor.

quiz.prompt: Health has replicated to a proxy. What should OnRep_Health do next?
choices: Play the local hit feedback and leave the float alone
Subtract Amount again so the proxy matches the hit
Top up ammo from the health notify
Start the interact trace
quiz.why: The server already applied the damage.

quiz.prompt: A client subtracts Health on its own machine when it sees a hit. What does the listen server show?
choices: A different health than that client, until a correction arrives
The same health immediately, because clients are trusted
Any client write should instantly kill the pawn
The server stops replicating that pawn
quiz.why: Two writers means two numbers.

quiz.prompt: Tick subtracts a point of health so damage feels continuous. What rule did that break?
choices: Health changes when damage happens
Speed must be zero before health can change
Only OnRep may write Health
Magazine and Health must stay equal
quiz.why: Tick would drain a pawn that nobody shot.

quiz.prompt: The health bar is a widget. Should the widget assign Health?
choices: No. It reads the replicated number and draws it
The drawn bar should be the number everyone trusts
Only remote pawns should let the widget assign health
Only when the mag is empty
quiz.why: UI listens.

quiz.prompt: True or false: clients may ask to be damaged, but they do not write Health.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Ask with an RPC. The authority writes.

quiz.prompt: True or false: OnRep_Health should subtract Amount a second time.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That applies the hit twice.

quiz.prompt: Two shots hit one pawn on the same server frame. Who produces the single Health everyone else will replicate?
choices: The authority, applying both hits in its order
The shooter with the lower ping
Each client, averaging the two guesses
The door the pawn is standing near
quiz.why: One writer.

quiz.prompt: True or false: making Health replicated lets every machine assign it.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Replication copies the authority's value. It does not elect a writer.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why may only the authority change Health when this pawn takes damage?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What do the listen server and the client disagree about if a client writes Health?

inventory.plainEnglish: Walking into a pickup asks the slot to take it. The slot owns the count. The use trace that opens doors does not also increment the stack.
inventory.whyGame: If the look trace adds items, staring at a crate fills your inventory. If the overlap forgets to clear the local count, the same volume adds the item again.

expansions.title: Ammo box
expansions.detail: The box overlaps, calls AddToSlot, and the slot adds reserve. The use key is not required.

expansions.title: Key
expansions.detail: A key is another slot id. The door's Interact later checks that slot. The overlap still only asks.

expansions.title: Full stack
expansions.detail: If the slot refuses a full stack, the pickup stays in the world. The count is not cleared.

quiz.prompt: The slot counts and the pickup asks. Which event is the ask?
choices: Begin Overlap on the pickup
The use key's line trace
Pressing reload should be what picks the item up
Scoring a medal should be what picks the item up
quiz.why: You walk into the item. You do not have to press use for this lesson's slot.

quiz.prompt: StackCount = 0 after a successful AddToSlot. What does that line prevent?
choices: The same overlap adding the item again
The magazine exceeding MagSize
Health replicating
The pawn sprinting
quiz.why: The local count is spent.

quiz.prompt: AddToSlot is called only when StackCount is greater than zero. What node is that check?
choices: Branch, in front of the interface call
Changing gait should gate the inventory add
Play From Start on the door timeline
An interest check should gate the inventory add
quiz.why: An empty overlap must not invent an item.

quiz.prompt: The use trace increments StackCount when it hits a crate. What does the player see?
choices: Inventory filling just by looking at the crate
A pickup only when they walk into it
The crate opening through Interact
Reserve moving into the magazine
quiz.why: The look is not the counter.

quiz.prompt: A medkit and an ammo box both use this slot pattern. What do they share?
choices: Overlap asks, and each item names its own slot
One StackCount for every item type in the game
The reload clamp
The fog Visible bit
quiz.why: The ask is shared. The slot id is not.

quiz.prompt: Who owns the number of medkits you are carrying?
choices: The inventory slot, after it accepts the add
The pickup actor, even after it is destroyed
The widget that draws the icon
The interact trace's hit result
quiz.why: The pickup asks. The slot counts.

quiz.prompt: True or false: overlap should call AddToSlot only when the stack count is positive.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Zero means there is nothing to give.

quiz.prompt: True or false: the use-key trace is what increments the inventory stack.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Use calls Interact. Overlap asks the slot.

quiz.prompt: The slot refuses because it is full. What should the pickup do?
choices: Stay in the world and keep its count
Destroy itself and delete the player's existing stack
Write Health to zero
Start a patrol
quiz.why: A refused add is not a successful transfer.

quiz.prompt: True or false: clearing StackCount before AddToSlot succeeds is the safe order.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Clear after the slot accepts, or a refused pickup vanishes.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does overlap, not the use trace, add a pickup to the slot?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What fills the bag if the look trace increments the stack while you stare at a crate?

gunsmith.plainEnglish: Equip writes one id, on the authority. Other machines build the visible gun from that id. The meshes themselves are not the replicated payload.
gunsmith.whyGame: Replicating every mesh and attachment is heavy, and a client that writes EquippedId outside HasAuthority makes proxies pop the wrong weapon.

expansions.title: Ten slots
expansions.detail: The ten weapons can live in a data asset. Only the equipped id has to replicate.

expansions.title: Skin
expansions.detail: A skin id can be a second replicated integer. It is still not the mesh pointer.

expansions.title: Drop
expansions.detail: Drop can clear the id on the authority. The pickup that appears is a different actor.

quiz.prompt: Replicate the id, not the meshes. What is the id in this graph?
choices: EquippedId, set from the equip action
How fast you move
The hunter's alert flag
Whether fog says you can be seen
quiz.why: The id picks the weapon. The meshes are local assets.

quiz.prompt: EquippedId = IA_Equip is nested inside HasAuthority. What does a client write outside that check cause?
choices: Other machines show a weapon the server did not equip
A faster equip, with the server copying the client
The magazine clamp to run
Fog to mark the player visible
quiz.why: The id is shared state.

quiz.prompt: IA_Equip fires. What runs before EquippedId changes?
choices: The authority check on the owning actor
A line trace from the muzzle
Filling the magazine
Reveal on the fog timer
quiz.why: No authority, no write.

quiz.prompt: You replicate the skeletal mesh pointer so everyone sees the right gun. What is the cheaper fact you should have sent?
choices: The equipped id, which each client turns into meshes locally
The player's ping
The door's IsOpen bool. A door flag does not say whether the magazine can take more rounds.
The stick axis
quiz.why: The id is small. The mesh is an asset the client already has.

quiz.prompt: Ten weapons sit in a data asset. A player equips slot 3. What do remote players need?
choices: The number 3, so they can look up the same asset
A replicated copy of all ten meshes every time
The reload Needed value
Alert set to 1
quiz.why: The asset stays local. The choice replicates.

quiz.prompt: OnRep of EquippedId plays the swap. Should it also assign a new id?
choices: No. It shows the weapon the authority already chose
The swap stays unfinished unless the notify writes a new id
The notify should write the magazine size into the weapon id
Only if the player is overlapping a pickup
quiz.why: OnRep performs. It does not decide.

quiz.prompt: True or false: EquippedId is written on the authority from the equip action.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the graph.

quiz.prompt: True or false: each equipped attachment mesh should be its own replicated object.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The id selects local assets.

quiz.prompt: A cheat sends an equip id the player does not own. Where is that refused?
choices: On the authority, before EquippedId is stored
On the widget, which is the only real check
Inside the interact miss log
Every frame should wipe the equipped id
quiz.why: The server owns the id.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Graph_IA_Equip runs when the player picks a weapon slot.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The function is the equip action.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does equip replicate one id instead of every mesh and attachment?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What do proxies show if a client writes EquippedId outside HasAuthority?

save.plainEnglish: Something that finished — a checkpoint, a menu save — packs one struct. Begin Play reads that struct back. Tick never writes the slot, because a value mid-change is not a save.
save.whyGame: Writing SlotValue from Health every frame stores a half-updated pawn and fights the next real event. Loading in the constructor is too early: the pawn and its components are not ready.

expansions.title: Checkpoint volume
expansions.detail: The volume calls the same save the menu uses. It does not invent a second struct.

expansions.title: Continue
expansions.detail: Continue is Begin Play reading the slot and applying health, ammo, and the equipped id.

expansions.title: Second slot
expansions.detail: Another slot is another save object, not a Tick that alternates two floats.

quiz.prompt: One struct is written on an event. Which event in this graph loads it?
choices: Begin Play
The per-frame update
The stick axis
Getting shot
quiz.why: Begin Play is the load. The write happened earlier, on purpose.

quiz.prompt: Graph_BeginPlay_tpl_saveload_begin runs. What is it allowed to do?
choices: Read the slot and apply the saved fields once
Trace for a use target
Subtract health
Step a patrol route
quiz.why: Load applies. It does not replay the actions that earned the numbers.

quiz.prompt: Make Struct packs the stand-in values. What node stores them on the slot?
choices: Set, writing SlotValue from the struct
Branch on a hit bool
Warming the barrel
The hunter's look timer
quiz.why: The struct is built, then stored.

quiz.prompt: Tick assigns SlotValue from Health every frame. What bad save does that produce?
choices: A snapshot taken in the middle of a change, including while the pawn is still falling
A perfect checkpoint only when the player asks. Tick would store the half-finished moment instead.
No file, because Tick cannot assign floats
A reload of the magazine
quiz.why: An event that finished is the save. A frame is not.

quiz.prompt: The player hits continue. Health, the mag, and EquippedId return together. Why one struct?
choices: So those fields load as one snapshot instead of three files that can disagree
Because a struct is the only type Tick can write
So OnRep can subtract them all
Because interfaces require a struct argument
quiz.why: One write, one load, one moment.

quiz.prompt: Loading in the constructor seems earlier and safer. Why is Begin Play the right time?
choices: The pawn and its components exist by Begin Play. They do not, reliably, in the constructor
Constructors cannot call functions
Begin Play runs only on clients
The constructor already traced the world. Actors and their components are not ready that early.
quiz.why: You apply the slot onto objects that are already there.

quiz.prompt: True or false: the save struct should be written when a save event finishes, not from Tick.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Tick catches values mid-change.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Begin Play should replay every shot that led to the saved magazine count.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Load applies the result. It does not resimulate the match.

quiz.prompt: A checkpoint volume and the pause menu both save. How many slot formats should they use?
choices: One struct, called from either place
Two structs, so the menu can store different fields than the volume
A Tick buffer plus a struct
No struct. Each system replicates its own mesh
quiz.why: Two writers of two shapes drift.

quiz.prompt: True or false: SlotValue = Health inside Tick is a valid checkpoint.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That line never waits for a finished event.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does a finished checkpoint pack the struct, while Tick never writes the slot?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What half-updated pawn gets stored if SlotValue is written from Health every frame?

fps-beginner-e6: Health replication should pick the sprint speed
